name: Naturalisation (Dutch citizenship)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 years of legal residence in the Netherlands. A previously-proposed increase to 10 years was dropped by the Jetten I coalition and is not law.
This requires a civic integration diploma or NT2 state exam at A2 level. A proposed increase to B1 is not yet law.
requirements.fix_path: Take the civic integration diploma or NT2 state exam at A2.

requirements.blocker_text: This generally requires renouncing your prior nationality, unless you qualify for an exemption (e.g. married to/registered partner of a Dutch citizen, recognised refugee status, born in the Netherlands, a national of a country that legally forbids renunciation such as Morocco or Argentina, mandatory military service, or disproportionate financial loss).
requirements.fix_path: Confirm exemption eligibility, or accept renunciation of your current nationality.

requirement_groups.name: Spouse or registered partner of a Dutch citizen

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 3 years of legal residence as the spouse or registered partner of a Dutch citizen (may also apply without residence in NL, or earlier, if married 3+ years to a Dutch national).
This requires a civic integration diploma or NT2 state exam at A2 level.
requirements.fix_path: Take the civic integration diploma or NT2 state exam at A2.

requirements.blocker_text: Being married to or the registered partner of a Dutch citizen is itself one of the standard exemptions from the renunciation requirement.

evidence_required.document: Civic integration diploma or NT2 state exam certificate at A2
Naturalisation ceremony attendance and declaration of solidarity

sources.title: Becoming a Dutch national through naturalisation - IND

notes: MAJOR LIVE POLICY EVENT confirmed, not pending: a proposal to extend the standard residence requirement from 5 to 10 years was DROPPED by the Jetten I coalition (confirmed via DutchNews.nl, January 2026, citing immigration lawyer Jeremy Bierbach) — the 5-year rule stands, and this is explicitly stated in the general route's blocker_text so a user doesn't have to guess whether an old headline about the 10-year proposal is still relevant. A proposed A2→B1 language increase (IND published an implementation assessment in February 2026) is likewise NOT yet law — same treatment, stated explicitly rather than silently encoded as if settled. dual_citizenship_allowed is false as the GENERAL rule, but the exemption list is genuinely substantial (married to a Dutch citizen, refugees, nationals of renunciation-forbidding countries like Morocco and Argentina, NL-born, military service, disproportionate financial loss) — worth surfacing prominently, since many applicants likely qualify for an exemption without realizing it, similar to Germany's dual-citizenship position but reached via exemptions rather than a blanket 2024 policy change. Fee €1,139 single / €1,454 joint / €168 minor confirmed via IND fee schedule — a tier-3 site's '€970' figure is stale. Both groups' outcome_override set citizenship_after_months to 0 since this route itself directly grants citizenship — the route-level default of 0 already matches, so overrides here are technically redundant but included for explicitness and consistency with how uk_citizenship and de_naturalisation handle the same pattern.
